scope: Books 3–4 locations and transition/shared settings; Books 1–5 project subset.
method: Official publisher descriptions and authorized samples anchor book/floor chronology. Granular names are paraphrased from secondary fan databases, often indexed because direct Fandom retrieval is blocked. No full novels supplied or exhaustively audited.
canonPolicy: canonSummary is source-supported paraphrase, not an independently verified full-text canon guarantee. All tile geometry, art colors beyond named route labels, tactical affordances, modular cuts and tilePieces are proposed art adaptations. Named routes are variants, not claims of unique architecture or visits. Fandom and DCCDatabase copies are not independent sources.

coverageGaps: Not an exhaustive full-text concordance. The Iron Tangle has hundreds of stations and 1,172 bubble environments exist; generic/unnamed locations are represented with reusable families rather than invented place names.

No exact spatial map reconstructed. Untangling the Iron Tangle is explicitly a fan model; repeated station numbers require route qualifiers. Do not make every occurrence of a number one unique global station.
Listed color routes are all 23 recovered from the indexed Fandom floor page, including passing mentions; individual party-visit status is unresolved for many colors.
Amaranth and Pink are reader-reported additional portal color labels (Book Three chapter 26); retained as pending candidates, not verified production canon.

Train yard A is described by an NPC as executive accommodation but wiki says it does not exist; do not depict it as a verified visited yard. Yard M is supported here only by indexed reader/podcast discussion and needs text confirmation.
Possible off-floor interlude places, every safe-room vendor, hotel name, exact Necropolis subroom names, and all neighboring-bubble biome differences need authorized full-text audit.
Pandinus proper name is confirmed by Gate wiki; commercial summary supplies Pazuzu settlement context. Exact architecture is adaptation.
Only remote Larracos consequences are within Book Four. No fully traversable Ninth-floor city, later temples or Faction Wars neighborhoods are justified by this scope.
Personal-space kitchen/kennel/magic upgrades appear as purchasable menu choices in Book Three sample; ownership timing beyond confirmed bed/shower/crafting/training is not inferred.
Odette studio is recurrent in Book Three epilogue; root shared-facilities inventory should merge its appearance and avoid duplicating a new floor-specific locale.
